messages:
Elaine: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — the canary miss yesterday exposed a few gaps. Need clear owners, short timelines, and a plan to reduce blast radius + enable safe auto-rollbacks.

Marc: I can take the auto-rollback POC. Idea: threshold-based rollback (error rate + latency spikes) with a short evaluation window. Will prototype on a staging canary.

Jess: I'll own tightening canary ramping rules and blast-radius caps. We should limit initial canary to <= 2% and do step increases only if health checks pass for X minutes.

Ravi: I'll add a small recurring check to detect patterns (same code path failing across rollouts) and surface when the same root cause appears >2 times in 30d.

Sam: Also needs an ops-runbook snippet for manual rollback steps + feature-flag kills. Keep it 1-2 commands so oncall can act quickly.

deploy-bot: [automated] Deploy record: deploy-2026-03-15-1422 by Marc -> started canary @5%

Marc: Proposal (config POC):
```yaml
canary:
  initial_pct: 0.02  # 2%
  step_pct: 0.05
  step_wait_s: 300  # 5min health window
  max_pct: 0.5
auto_rollback:
  enabled: true
  error_rate_threshold: 0.05
  window_s: 30
  min_canary_users: 50
  roll_forward_on_fix: false
```
Keep it simple for the POC. If error_rate >5% for 30s we trigger rollback.

Jess: Agreed. For blast radius control I want a guardrail: `max_blast_pct: 0.03` for feature flags tied to model weights. Also add a hard cap so a mis-ramped release can't push >cap.

Elaine: Action list (short):
- A1: Auto-rollback POC (Marc) — owner Marc, prototype deployed to test canary, validate rollback behavior, instrument metrics. Target: end of next week.
- A2: Canary ramp + blast-radius policy (Jess) — codify limits, add enforcement in deploy agent, add unit tests for ramp logic. Target: 2 weeks.
- A3: Recurring-pattern detector (Ravi) — surface repeated regressions and attach related rollouts, create alert. Target: 3 weeks.
- A4: Ops runbook + one-line kill commands (Sam) — doc + dry-run with oncall. Target: 5 business days.
- A5: Postmortem doc update (Elaine) — list owners, timelines, and link to PRs; ticket every 2 weeks until closed.

Marc: I'll open the POC PR tonight: branch `infra/auto-rollback-poc` and drop a short test harness that simulates error bursts.

Jess: I'll add the blast-radius enforcement to the deploy-agent config and a small e2e that fails if initial_pct > configured cap.

Ravi: For recurring patterns I'll start with a simple signal: group by stacktrace + model-id + route, then count occurrences in 30d. If count>=2 fire a pager (low severity) to SRE + owners.

Sam: I'll author the runbook and include the following minimal commands:
```bash
# kill canary traffic
redwood-cli rollout update --id <rollout-id> --canary-pct 0
# disable feature flag
redwood-cli flags set <flag> false
```
Keep these in the runbook with copyable snippets.

Elaine: One more governance point — add a required review by Reliability before any canary percent >10% for the next quarter. That should reduce risky fast ramps until automated checks mature.

Marc: 👍 I'll include a guard in the agent: if canary_pct_request > 0.1 and reliability_approval != true then fail the deploy with a clear message.

Jess: Also recommend a dashboard widget for the last 7 days showing rollbacks triggered by auto-rollback so we can tune thresholds and avoid noisy rollbacks.

Ravi: I'll surface the recurring-pattern detector results into that same dashboard to correlate.

Elaine: Sounds good. I'll capture these A-items in the postmortem doc and create a follow-up ticket board. We'll review status in next eng-platform sync. If anyone needs to reassign, ping me.

Marc: PR coming tonight.

Jess: Starting the enforcement work tomorrow morning.

Ravi: Picking up telemetry tasks after current sprint lock.

Sam: Runbook draft by EOD Wed for dry-run.

Elaine: Thanks all — closing the thread here, will update the postmortem with owners/due dates and link PRs. :thumbsup:
